title: Real Quadratic Fields: The Unit-Rank-One Case of Hilbert's 12th
description: Real quadratic fields are exactly the totally real degree-2 number fields; they have unit rank 1, distinguishing them from the CM-solved imaginary quadratic case (rank 0). Their regulator collapses to a single bare logarithm of the fundamental (Stark) unit — with no multiplicity factor.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 12th problem (Kronecker's Jugendtraum) asks for explicit generators of the abelian extensions of a number field K. It is solved for K = ℚ (Kronecker–Weber: roots of unity) and for imaginary quadratic K (complex multiplication: singular moduli and elliptic units). The **first genuinely open case** is the family of real quadratic fields ℚ(√d), d > 0 — the focus of this entry. The modern conjectural framework is the **Stark conjectures**, whose most-tested instance, the rank-one abelian Stark conjecture, applies exactly when the relevant unit rank is 1.
overview.problemStatement:
**Problem (parent oq-01):** Generators for abelian extensions of real quadratic fields.

**This entry** isolates the unit-theoretic reason real quadratic fields are the first open case. Abstractly a real quadratic field is a totally real number field of degree 2. It machine-checks that such fields have unit rank 1 (hence a fundamental/Stark unit and an infinite unit group), that the complementary imaginary quadratic degree-2 fields have unit rank 0 (the CM-solved case), and that the real quadratic regulator is a single bare logarithm of the fundamental unit.
overview.text: Among degree-2 number fields, the totally real ones (real quadratic) have unit rank 1 and their regulator is |log|ε|| for the fundamental (Stark) unit ε; the non-totally-real ones (imaginary quadratic) have unit rank 0. This unit-rank jump is exactly what separates the open real quadratic case of Hilbert's 12th from the CM-solved imaginary quadratic case.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. **Place count.** The place counts obey #(InfinitePlace K) = nrReal + nrComplex and nrReal + 2·nrComplex = [K : ℚ]. Feeding [K : ℚ] = 2 and (for the real case) nrComplex = 0 to `omega` fixes #(InfinitePlace K) = 2 (`card_infinitePlace_eq_two`).

2. **Rank.** Since rank K = #(InfinitePlace K) − 1 (Dirichlet), the real case gives rank 1 (`rank_eq_one`) and the imaginary case (nrComplex ≠ 0, forcing nrComplex = 1, nrReal = 0, #place = 1) gives rank 0 (`rank_eq_zero_of_not_isTotallyReal`). The equivalence `rank_eq_one_iff_isTotallyReal` packages the dichotomy.

3. **Regulator collapse.** For the real case, transport the `Unique (Fin (rank K))` instance (rank = 1) along `equivFinRank` and apply `Matrix.det_unique` to `regulator_eq_det`, reducing the regulator determinant to its single 1×1 entry mult(w)·|log w(ε)|; then `IsTotallyReal.mult_eq` sets mult w = 1, leaving the bare logarithm |log w(ε)| (`regulator_eq_single_log`).
keyInsights: Real quadratic vs imaginary quadratic is a unit-rank distinction: rank 1 vs rank 0. This — not the field degree — is why the imaginary case is CM-solved while the real case is the first open case of Hilbert's 12th.
The real/imaginary dichotomy is captured exactly by total reality: among degree-2 fields, rank K = 1 ⟺ IsTotallyReal K.

Total reality sharpens the rank-one regulator collapse: because mult w = 1 at every real place, the real quadratic regulator is a bare |log|ε||, unlike the mixed-signature cubic rank-one case which carries a multiplicity 2 from its complex place.

The fundamental unit ε (fundSystem K) is the Stark unit of the rank-one abelian Stark conjecture; this entry pins its regulator shape but does not address the open effective generation of abelian extensions.
prerequisites: Dirichlet's unit theorem: unit rank r₁ + r₂ − 1 = #(InfinitePlace K) − 1.
Signature (r₁, r₂) of a number field and its infinite places.
The regulator as the covolume of the unit lattice / a determinant of logarithms.
Stark conjectures (rank-one abelian case) for the L-function interpretation.

sections.title: Real Quadratic Fields: The First Open Case
sections.summary: The module docstring frames Hilbert's 12th problem — solved for ℚ (Kronecker–Weber) and imaginary quadratic fields (complex multiplication) — and identifies real quadratic fields ℚ(√d), d > 0, as the first genuinely open case. It explains the reason is unit-theoretic: imaginary quadratic fields have unit rank 0 (only roots of unity) while real quadratic fields have unit rank 1 (an infinite unit group with a fundamental unit), placing the latter in the Stark regime. It scopes the file to provable structural facts, excluding the open effective generation problem, and lists the five theorems and proof strategy.

sections.title: Two Infinite Places
sections.summary: card_infinitePlace_eq_two: a totally real degree-2 field has exactly two infinite places (both real). From nrComplex = 0 (total reality), #(InfinitePlace K) = nrReal + nrComplex and nrReal + 2·nrComplex = [K:ℚ] = 2, `omega` fixes the count at 2.

sections.title: Unit Rank One (Real Quadratic)
sections.summary: rank_eq_one: a totally real degree-2 field has unit rank 1. Since rank K = #(InfinitePlace K) − 1 by Dirichlet's unit theorem and the field has two infinite places, `rw [rank]; omega` gives rank 1 — the source of the fundamental (Stark) unit.

sections.title: The Imaginary Quadratic Complement (Rank Zero)
sections.summary: rank_eq_zero_of_not_isTotallyReal: a degree-2 field that is not totally real is imaginary quadratic with unit rank 0. Non-total-reality gives nrComplex ≠ 0; with nrReal + 2·nrComplex = 2 this forces nrComplex = 1, nrReal = 0, one infinite place, hence rank 0 — the CM-solved case.

sections.title: The Real/Imaginary Dichotomy
sections.summary: rank_eq_one_iff_isTotallyReal: among degree-2 number fields, unit rank 1 (real quadratic, the open Hilbert-12 case) holds exactly when the field is totally real; the rank-0 complement is the CM-solved imaginary quadratic case. Proved by combining rank_eq_one and rank_eq_zero_of_not_isTotallyReal with omega.

sections.title: Regulator = A Single Bare Logarithm
sections.summary: regulator_eq_single_log: for a totally real degree-2 field the regulator equals |log w(ε)| — a single archimedean logarithm of the fundamental (Stark) unit, with NO multiplicity factor. Reproves the rank-one collapse inline from regulator_eq_det on the equivFinRank-transported singleton via Matrix.det_unique, then kills the multiplicity via IsTotallyReal.mult_eq (mult w = 1 at a real place), sharpening the general rank-one collapse where a complex place would contribute a factor 2.

conclusion.summary: Five machine-checked results isolate the unit-theoretic reason real quadratic fields are the first open case of Hilbert's 12th problem. Abstractly a real quadratic field is a totally real degree-2 number field; such fields have exactly two infinite places and unit rank 1, while the complementary imaginary quadratic fields have unit rank 0. The dichotomy rank K = 1 ⟺ IsTotallyReal K captures this among all degree-2 fields, and the real quadratic regulator collapses to the bare logarithm |log w(ε)| of the fundamental (Stark) unit ε — sharper than the general rank-one collapse, which a complex place would burden with a multiplicity 2. 131 lines, 5 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), self-contained.
conclusion.implications: This makes precise why the imaginary quadratic case of Hilbert's 12th is solved (CM theory, unit rank 0) while the real quadratic case is open (unit rank 1, an infinite fundamental unit driving the Stark regime). It sharpens the sibling rank-one regulator collapse (oq-02) exactly on the real quadratic branch, exhibiting the regulator as one clean logarithm of the fundamental unit — the shape the rank-one abelian Stark conjecture predicts for L'(0, χ). It cleanly separates the verified structural fact from the genuinely open arithmetic: effectively generating the abelian extensions of a real quadratic field.
openQuestions: Relate the bare regulator |log w(ε)| to the L-function side: state and (conditionally) connect L'(0, χ) to log|ε| for the rank-one abelian Stark conjecture over a real quadratic base, making ε the Stark unit predicted by the L-value.
Produce explicit numerical witnesses of the real quadratic regulator formula for concrete ℚ(√d), where ε is the classical fundamental unit.

Address the open effective-generation problem: exhibit, for a real quadratic field, an explicit generator of a nontrivial abelian extension — the actual content of Hilbert's 12th problem in this first open case.
